D-035.text: **Adversarial code scans are capped at three runs per PR; QA repeats until it passes.** The owner's rule: "hard capping any adversarial agent reviews at 3 runs for code scans, and be more than willing to defer or ignore out of scope requests for PRs"; "that does not apply to QA runs, which can run indefinitely until they pass". Cross-vendor reviews and Astra audit rounds count together per PR. After the third, no further adversarial run is launched: in-scope blockers are fixed with Fable's review and green CI, out-of-scope requests become follow-up issues or are set aside, and the PR merges with the dispositions recorded here. PRs already past the cap on this date (#382 with ten reviews and one audit, #372 with four audits, G2's PR with three audits) stop their review loops now; #382 keeps one Astra audit round as its gate because its single audit round is the owner's requested mechanism and is within the cap for audits. Behaviour QA against the built app is exempt. This bounds D-029.

D-042.text: **Owner steering for the rest of I01 to I07: delivery merges everything in scope; the gate is an independent audit, bounded by D-035.** The orchestrator implements, fixes, integrates, commits, pushes, arranges independent review and QA, and merges all remaining in-scope work (the original seven intents, 21 UoWs and 59 nondeferred bolts; I08/I09, deferred children and unrelated backlog stay parked) when its technical gates pass, without per-PR owner permission. This supersedes the owner-only holds on PRs #355 and #375 (CP-21 to CP-66, the "waiting on the owner" lines and the WP-B3 no-verdict entry) and every remaining statement that only session `01a156ac-2e81-7d22-bce7-e6fe79719a41` can sign off (section 1, D-024, #278/#279), which D-029 had already replaced in this register. The gate is D-029's: a fresh independent auditor reviews the exact current head and target and its explicit `SIGN-OFF` is the technical gate. The orchestrator may write and issue every audit brief, including PR #375's (previously refused as self-approval); writing a brief is not a sign-off, an interrupted, filtered or refused audit has no verdict, and this instruction is not a technical sign-off. D-035's three-scan cap is never reset by a new head, thread or reviewer; at the cap the orchestrator fixes the known in-scope blockers, reviews the fixes, obtains independent behaviour QA and green CI, records the capped disposition and merges; no known in-scope blocker is waived. Counts reconciled on this date: **PR #355** has had well over three adversarial scans (Sol reviews `review-wp-b3`, `-2`, `-audit` to `-audit-9`; the Astra audit of `32568edd` ended in the provider's content filter with no verdict), so it takes the capped path; **PR #375** has had one (the orchestrator's cross-vendor review of #320); #321's code inside it was signed off in PR #377 (five Astra rounds) and is not re-counted, so #375 has two audit rounds left. A tool or permission refusal is reported exactly and never routed around; owner authorization does not disable a permission checker; a content-filter failure is neither approval nor permission to evade it. Delivery never resets, deletes, upgrades or restarts the owner's checkout, app or store (ports 4747/4748, `~/.graphgoblin`); this ends the owner-instance upgrades after merges (CP-49 to CP-66), and register commits are made from a separate worktree. Gates run on a project-scoped Node v22.23.4 (`~/.claude/codex-runs/GraphGoblin/runtime`), which meets D-039's patch floor without changing the machine's runtime. Human QA is the owner's, after the integrated work merges: objectively verifiable criteria are completed through independent agents, genuine judgement calls get an explicit open post-merge QA item, and "engineering merged and verified" is recorded separately from "human QA complete".
